items.stem: What does the Fargate launch type remove the need to manage, compared with the EC2 launch type?

options.rationale: Correct: Fargate runs tasks without you provisioning or patching EC2 hosts.
You still define tasks on Fargate.
You still build and supply images.
IAM roles are still required for tasks.

items.explanation: Correct: Fargate runs tasks without you provisioning or patching EC2 hosts.

items.stem: What is the safest way to give a container access to a database password in ECS?

options.text: Reference it from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store in the task definition
options.rationale: Correct: referencing a managed secret avoids embedding credentials in the image.

options.text: Hard-code it in the container image
options.rationale: Baking credentials into an image is insecure and hard to rotate.

options.text: Print it to the container logs
Store it in the task name
options.rationale: Task names are not a secret store.

items.explanation: Correct: referencing a managed secret avoids embedding credentials in the image.

items.stem: Which TWO are true when running ECS tasks in awsvpc network mode? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Each task gets its own elastic network interface
options.rationale: Correct: awsvpc gives each task a dedicated ENI.

options.text: Security groups can be applied at the task level
options.rationale: Correct: tasks can have their own security groups in awsvpc mode.

options.text: Tasks must use bridge-mode port mappings
options.rationale: Bridge mode is a different, incompatible networking mode.

options.text: Tasks cannot be placed behind a load balancer
options.rationale: awsvpc tasks integrate with load balancers.

items.explanation: Correct: awsvpc gives each task its own ENI and task-level security groups.
